<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="מנחם אב_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518919765_theRebbe_137" batchId="meluket-_D7_9E_D7_A0_D7_97_D7_9D_20_D7_90_D7_91_meluket__BH_POST_1766518919765_theRebbe_137__p005">
  <section v="12">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>Even the nullification of faith, which is above intellect, is not total nullification, because it stems from a feeling of G-dliness in the soul, analogous to a light that senses its source.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">6)</t>
    <t s="1">Now, even the nullification of faith, which is above intellect, is not total nullification.</t>
    <t s="2">For the nullification of faith is that one believes in G-dliness even though from the perspective of his intellect</t>
    <t s="3">(his existence)</t>
    <t s="4">he has no proofs of this.</t>
    <t s="5">And since the reason for this—that he believes in G-dliness</t>
    <t s="6">(even though he has no proofs of this)</t>
    <t s="7">—is that G-dliness is felt in his soul</t>
    <t s="8">[except that this feeling is above his existence</t>
    <t s="9">(comprehension)</t>
    <t s="10">],</t>
    <t s="11">therefore,</t>
    <t s="12">the nullification of faith is not total nullification,</t>
    <t s="13">because he believes because G-dliness is felt within him.</t>
    <t s="14">And this is analogous to the nullification of light by its sensing its source</t>
    <t s="15">(the essence of the luminary),</t>
    <t s="16">for even though this sensing of its source is above its existence</t>
    <t s="17">[for the essence of the luminary is not revealed in the light],</t>
    <t s="18">nevertheless,</t>
    <t s="19">this is sensed in the light as it is in its existence,</t>
    <t s="20">an existence outside the source</t>
    <t s="21">[therefore,</t>
    <t s="22">this sensing of its source does not cause it to desire to be included in its source].</t>
    <t s="23">And the nullification of self-sacrifice,</t>
    <t s="24">where one gives his soul for the sake of G-dliness</t>
    <t s="25">(departure from his existence),</t>
    <t s="26">is analogous to the nullification of light from the aspect of its ratzo to be included in its source.</t>
    <t s="27">This is also understood from the continuation of the topics in Tanya36,</t>
    <t s="28">that the power of self-sacrifice in Israel is analogous to the desire of the soul to separate and depart from the body and cleave to its root and source,</t>
    <t s="29">even though it will become naught and nothing and be nullified there in existence entirely37.</t>
    <t s="30">And to add,</t>
    <t s="31">that in the desire of the soul to be included in Ein Sof, there are two levels.</t>
    <t s="32">That it wants to be included,</t>
    <t s="33">and that it is in a state of dissolution in a spontaneous manner.</t>
    <t s="34">And it can be said,</t>
    <t s="35">that since the nullification</t>
    <t s="36">(of light)</t>
    <t s="37">that comes from the desire to be included in its source is total nullification</t>
    <t s="38">(like the nullification of light included in the luminary as mentioned above in section 3),</t>
    <t s="39">therefore the desire is also nullified.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="13">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>The ratzo of light to be included in its source exists in all levels of light, but its primary manifestation is in the essence of light above the category of enclothing in vessels.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">7)</t>
    <t s="1">And the maamar continues38,</t>
    <t s="2">that since the ratzo of light to be included in its source is because it is attached to its source,</t>
    <t s="3">therefore,</t>
    <t s="4">the ratzo of light</t>
    <t s="5">[and likewise the nullification that comes from ratzo]</t>
    <t s="6">exists in all levels of light,</t>
    <t s="7">even in the light that is enclothed in vessels</t>
    <t s="8">(for the fact that light is attached to its source is in all its levels),</t>
    <t s="9">except that the primary ratzo</t>
    <t s="10">[and the nullification that comes from ratzo]</t>
    <t s="11">is in the essence of light, which is above the category of enclothing in vessels.</t>
    <t s="12">And it can be said,</t>
    <t s="13">that in the nature of the ratzo in light to be included in its source,</t>
    <t s="14">there are two matters.</t>
    <t s="15">The desire to be included in its source,</t>
    <t s="16">and the desire not to be outside its source.</t>
    <t s="17">And that the primary ratzo is in the essence of light,</t>
    <t s="18">is,</t>
    <t s="19">that in the light that is enclothed in vessels and in the category of enclothing,</t>
    <t s="20">it is the desire not to be outside its source,</t>
    <t s="21">and in the essence of light, it is the desire to be included in its source.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="14">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>Each of the two desires in light has a unique advantage: the desire to be included is loftier, while the desire not to be outside is more internal and present in all levels.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And the explanation is,</t>
    <t s="1">that regarding these two desires mentioned above, each one has an advantage that the other lacks.</t>
    <t s="2">The desire to be included in its source is more elevated,</t>
    <t s="3">for this desire in light is because the source is sensed in it—and the revelation of the source is primarily in the essence of light.</t>
    <t s="4">And the desire not to be outside its source is more internal</t>
    <t s="5">(deeper)</t>
    <t s="6">in the light,</t>
    <t s="7">to the extent that this desire is in the very essence of its existence—and therefore it is in all its levels.</t>
    <t s="8">And this is analogous to the distinction between the soul's desire to be included in Ein Sof and the power of self-sacrifice39,</t>
    <t s="9">that the desire to be included in Ein Sof is revealed only in unique individuals,</t>
    <t s="10">while the matter of self-sacrifice—not to be separated, G-d forbid, from G-dliness—is revealed in every single person.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
